cultivar: Various Dancong strains, such as Wu Ye
processing: Winter leaf made as Dancong, usually with light oxidation that keeps the leaf quite green. Winter leaf grows slowly and comes out stout.
harvest_season: The last picking of the year, around November.
appearance_dry: Stout, coarse-looking strips, usually greener than spring Dancong.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold, lighter than a typical spring Dancong, as is expected from light oxidation.
appearance_wet: Fairly green leaves, reflecting the light oxidation.
taste_profile: Intensely aromatic, with fruit and flowers and a creamy mouthfeel.

brewing.notes: Slightly cooler water than for roasted Dancong protects the aroma; this is a general rule for lightly oxidised oolongs.

vintage_note: Sold as the winter harvest of a stated year, in small lots and usually as a single named strain, for example Wu Ye or Ya Shi Xiang. Being lightly oxidised, it is best drunk fresh, like other greener oolongs. Note that sellers also offer black teas under the snowflake name, so check the category.
description:
Xue Pian, snowflake, is less a strain than a season: the last Dancong picking of the year, taken around November from whichever Fenghuang strain the maker works with.

Cold weather slows the leaf, so it comes out stout, and yields are the lowest of any Dancong picking. Makers usually oxidise it lightly, which is why the leaf stays comparatively green.

The appeal is pure aroma: fruit and flowers on a creamy texture. Treat it more gently than a roasted spring Dancong, with slightly cooler water and quick pours.

Because Xue Pian describes a picking, the label should name the strain as well as the year. Small harvests invite stretching the name, so buy from someone who can say which trees it came from.
history: Little is documented about when the name came into use. Chinese descriptions of the Wu Ye strain explain it as the winter picking, named for its stout flake-like leaf and prized as the scarcest and most fragrant of the year. Today it is sold abroad as well, usually as a named winter lot.
